title: Oklahoma Center of Medical Imaging for Translational Cancer Research
text:
Overall Significance to Public Health (Project Narrative)
 The overarching objective of this COBRE application is to establish a new biomedical imaging research
center with appropriate infrastructure and research capacity along with a multidisciplinary mentoring team to
support the promising research project leaders of junior investigators as they conduct the innovative translational
cancer research projects using advanced medical imaging technology. The success of this COBRE will ultimately
have a high research and clinical impact lead to a reduced cancer burden both for individual patients and society
as a whole.

title: Artificial Intelligence and Counterfactually Actionable Responses to End HIV (AI-CARE-HIV)
text:
PROJECT NARRATIVE / PUBLIC HEALTH RELEVANCE
Antiretroviral therapy (ART) for people with Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV) can successfully bring down
viral load, minimize infectiousness, and improve quality of life. Despite availability of ART subsidization in the
US, several states including Florida experience high prevalence of virological failures, HIV comorbidity, with
enormous racial and social disparity in ART outcomes. Fusion of causal inference and artificial intelligence
methods, in conjunction with real-world multilevel data (e.g., electronic health records, social determinants of
health) and expert-designed interventions, is key to develop models that can be actioned to improve ART
outcomes and reduce disparity.

title: Core-003
text: The Duke Regional Biocontainment Laboratory was commissioned in 2007 as a part of a network of 12 RBLs tasked with providing state-of-the-art facilities to aid in the response emerging pathogens and pandemic preparedness. This grant will provide critical support of the RBL operational infrastructure, comprehensive training program, and enhancement of Research Support services.

title: Elucidating properties of T cell receptors that govern pancreatic cancer immunotherapy response
text:
This project aims to elucidate traits of T cell receptors that promote T cell fitness and immunotherapy response
in pancreatic cancer. Our work will guide TCR selection and combinatorial strategies to enhance T cell
therapies against solid tumors, ultimately yielding a significant impact for the field.

title: Research Training in Cell and Molecular Biology
text: The UCLA Cell and Molecular Biology (CMB) Training Program endeavors to train and prepare the next generation of cell and molecular biology PhD students for biomedical careers. The underpinnings of the CMB Training Program come from the interdisciplinary state-of-the-art research training in cellular and molecular biology provided by the CMB student-centered curriculum, structured-activities, and faculty mentors. Additionally, the CMB Training Program provides skill development and career development training, while supporting trainees through mentoring and cohort-building activities.

title: Understanding the variability in nonsense-mediated RNA decay
text:
All cells have surveillance mechanisms to detect and degrade aberrant RNAs carrying nonsense
mutations. The goal of my research program is to characterize the factors that induce variability
in RNA surveillance. Better understanding of this variation will improve the clinical interpretation
of genetic variants, and may help identify novel therapeutic approaches to counter genetic
disorders.

title: Core C-Research Computing, Bioinformatics, and Biostatistics
text: Core C-Abstract The Molecular Center of Health and Disease (MCHD) will facilitate research under a central theme of molecular physiology to enhance the depth of education, mentorship, and training of researchers to apply omics technology and computational biology across the health-disease continuum. Research aimed at understanding genetic susceptibility and molecular mechanisms involved in disease onset has the potential to halt progression and return an individual to a healthier state. As advances in technology have allowed for insight into genomic, transcriptomic, proteomic, and metabolomic complexity, the need to develop computational biology approaches to integrate and merge these omics datasets along with physiological data (in total systems biology) has become critical. In total, computational approaches applied to molecular, cellular, and overall pathophysiology associated with the health-disease continuum can provide important systems biology level information. The mission of the MCHD will be achieved through synergistic interaction across multiple components including Core A (administrative oversight, education and mentoring programs, and a pilot project program), two research cores, and three major project investigators to address diverse questions of health and disease using molecule and computational approaches. In particular, Core C- Research Computing, Bioinformatics, and Biostatistics will provide researchers access to high-performance research computing infrastructure, custom bioinformatics analysis pipelines and biostatistical support. Core C will leverage the comprehensive state-of-the-art omics data collection pipeline and mechanistic gene-editing and biological approaches from Core B to provide major project and pilot investigators unique insight into the health-disease continuum. Core C will build new computing infrastructure at the University, provide vital bioinformatics and computational biology analysis, facilitate a novel “Bioinformatics and Data Sciences Collaborative”, and leverage and expand current biostatistics services available through the School of Population Health. The objective of Core C is: (1) provide education and training opportunities for faculty, trainees, and students in research computing and computational biology approaches; (2) establish an innovative research computing infrastructure required for analyses of large omics datasets via standard and custom analyses pipelines to return biologically relevant analyses to MCHD investigators; (3) provide MCHD investigators access to biostatistical expertise and services for optimal experimental design, statistical analyses, and interpretation of findings; and (4) to seek continuous improvement in research computing infrastructure, services, and enhance analytical capabilities through implementation of new approaches, algorithms, and methodology to assist in the sustainability of the Core. In total, through close coordination with Core B, this core will establish, grow, and sustain infrastructure to enhance and build systems biology focused approaches to the health and disease continuum, bring together multidisciplinary expertise to support innovative extramural research applications of junior investigators, and collaboratively cultivate the success of the MCHD.

title: Ceramide metabolism and the regulation of PD-L1 signaling to control metastasis and resistance to immunotherapy in TNBC
text:
The main goals of this project are to define mechanisms that regulate PD-L1 internalization and intrinsic signaling
to develop novel therapeutic approaches and overcome immunotherapy resistance in metastatic TNBC.

title: Promoting Functional Neuromuscular Regeneration Following Chronic VML in Aged Mice
text:
In this study, we will establish a model of chronic volumetric muscle loss (VML) injuries in middle-aged C57BL/6J
mice to phenocopy the clinical scenario. We will incorporate advanced lightsheet imaging and multi-tissue
transcriptomics to elucidate neuromuscular deficits and cellular cross-talk in response to VML injury. Data and
insights from these studies will inform the design of novel pro-regenerative biomaterials to restore functional
neuromuscular junctions in regenerated skeletal muscle.

title: Toward vocal fold scar mitigation through CRISPR/Cas-9-mediated gene editing of fibroblasts
text:
Voice disorders affect nearly 30% of Americans at some point during their lifetime. Vocal fold scarring, a
common cause of voice disorders, lacks a consistent and reliable treatment. In this research proposal, we seek
to use specific vocal fold cells, called fibroblasts, to identify possible genetic targets to reduce vocal fold
scarring using novel approaches - CRISPR/Cas9 gene editing and RNA sequencing.

title: An Adaptive Intervention to Increase Engagement to Community-based Care After an ED Admission: For Youth Aged 10 to 14 at Risk for Suicide and Self-injurious Behavior
text:
The goal of this application is to explore the development and feasibility of a brief, family-based adaptive
intervention, via SMART design, for youth 10 to 14 years with suicidal and non-suicidal self-injurious behavior
(SSIB) to increase community-based mental health (MH) care attendance and reduce SSIB risk post emergency
department (ED) admission. The intervention will focus to increase understanding on youth MH literacy, MH
communication, and MH engagement. Integrating an adaptive intervention via a SMART design in the ED could
address subsequent barriers to youth obtaining appropriate level of community-based MH care and therefore
reduce ED readmissions.

title: Dual imaging of pHi and pHe to dissociate glycolytic/oxidative phenotypes for novel GBM therapeutics
text:
Given that a key resistance mechanism in cancer therapy is the acidity inherent to tumor
microenvironment, we propose to develop a novel imaging technique that can visualize at high resolution the
acidity inside tumor cells in relation to acidity of their environment. Targeting the acid extruding mechanisms
responsible for controlling the acidity of internal and external compartments of tumor cells has shown promising
results as novel anti-cancer therapeutic strategy because tumor’s survival and function depend on making the
extracellular tumor environment more acidic and intracellular tumor environment more alkaline (i.e. less acidic).
This method will help us better understand the resistance mechanisms in cancer and it can be used to monitor
therapy response and disease progression, and guide therapeutic decisions for improved personalized cancer
therapy.

title: Mechanistic studies of CRISPR immunity and DNAmethylation
text:
The proposed research is relevant to public health because it will increase our understanding of
(1) how bacteria protect themselves from phage infection and (2) how DNA methylation in
humans is regulated. Our studies will define the molecular mechanisms that govern these
processes. Results from these studies will contribute to the development of novel molecular
tools and lay the ground work for improving the control of disease.

title: Development of novel AAV vaccine strategy in a pre-clinical model of oral melanoma.
text:
Our study expected to validate novel vaccine in dogs with spontaneous oral melanoma and gain better
understanding towards possible use of viral-based immunotherapy in human patients, which has direct relevance
to public health.

title: Understanding evasion of cell intrinsic innate immunity in viral populations with high rates of replicative failure
text:
A key component of success for most viruses is the antagonisim of the production of interferons,
potent signaling proteins that drive the induction of an antiviral state. Critically, viruses must maintain this
antagonism throughout all members of the the population, as detection of any single viral particle and
subsequent interferon production endangers them all. This proposal seeks to understand how this difficult
challenge is achieved by influenza A virus in the face of highly promiscuous replication machinery, in the
hopes that such an understanding may provide insight into novel therapeutic targets as well as an improved
understanding of viral evolution.

title: Environmental-use chemicals that target pathways linked to autism and other neurodevelopmental disorders
text:
Unlike de novo gene mutations, which cannot be avoided, chemical exposures can be minimized or eliminated,
particularly during critical periods of brain development. Our research will evaluate thousands of chemicals,
including mixtures, and identify those with the greatest potential to impact neurodevelopmental processes.
This new knowledge will enable us and others to evaluate real-world risks associated with these
chemicals/mixtures, permit future generations to minimize exposure, and help to reduce the prevalence of
avoidable neurodevelopmental disorders—those that are caused or exacerbated by chemical risks.

title: miR-21 regulation of autoreactive B cell and lupus nephritis development
text:
This proposal focuses on developing a comprehensive understanding of the mechanism by which miR-21, an
miRNA that is strongly associated with mouse and human SLE but yet poorly characterized, drives
autoimmune responses and lupus nephritis. We will learn how an interplay of miR-21 and TLR7 signaling
regulates B cell activation and metabolism in TLR7-promoted SLE. Finally, we will learn whether miR-21 or
miR-21 regulated pathway(s) can be a therapeutic target for SLE.

title: Treatment of Multidrug-Resistant Staphylococcus aureus Orthopaedic-Device Related Biofilm Infections with Local Delivery of Lytic Bacteriophage
text:
Device-related infections are a major complication in orthopaedic medicine
resulting in a large economic burden, significant patient morbidity, and are increasingly difficult
to treat because as biofilm infections, they are resistant to antibiotics and the host immune
system. An emerging strategy to treat other types of antibiotic- and multidrug-resistant infections
is to directly target and lyse the bacterial pathogen using IV-administration of bacteriophage
(viruses that kill bacteria) or `phage'. As IV phage administration has drawbacks for phage
treatment of orthopaedic device-related infections (ODRIs), including the loss of phage during
delivery and long-term exposure to the immune system, we propose here an innovative
nanotechnology strategy using a biodegradable microsphere delivery system, originally
developed to deliver antibiotics, to locally administer lytic phage to treat ODRIs and eventually
improve patient outcomes.

title: Mechanisms of membrane homeostasis through protein and lipid transport
text:
Membrane biogenesis is an essential process for all living cells and defects in this process underlies
many of the most common human diseases. Moreover, the majority of drugs in the market target
membrane proteins or membrane-associated processes. This research will improve our
understanding of how biological membranes are assembled and how they achieve their precise
composition of lipid and protein molecules.

title: Mechanisms of mGlu1 regulation of cortical inhibition and cognitive function: Implications in adolescent cocaine exposure
text:
Early onset cocaine use during critical neurodevelopmental periods like adolescence is associated with
pronounced cognitive deficits later in life which are paralleled by neurobiological changes in the prefrontal cortex
(PFC). Therefore, we propose a series of studies aimed at testing the hypothesis that physiological and cognitive
deficits associated with adolescent cocaine exposure are mediated by the mGlu1 subtype of metabotropic
glutamate (mGlu) receptor on specific neuron populations in the PFC. Results from these studies will enhance
our understanding of the neurobiology underlying neurodevelopmental consequences related to early onset
cocaine exposure and will aid in efforts to develop mGlu receptor modulators as novel medications to treat
cocaine use disorder.
